Risk Premia: Final Research Dashboard

Five commodity asset classes, four sleeves each (Momentum, Carry, Carry-Momentum, Value), combined by Equal Weight and Inverse Vol only. Log-return methodology, 5 bps costs, reporting from 2011-01-01. All price data through 2026-09-23. Generated 2026-10-11.

Method, data and what changed

Sleeves (per product)

  • Momentum: average of the signs of three moving-average crossovers, (1,20), (5,60), (20,250), on the raw front-month price; 1-day lag.
  • Carry (V2): z-score of the carry slope, (near - far) / near, against its own trailing 252 days. With two tenor pairs, each pair gives a sign and the two signs are averaged then signed again (sign-vote): the position is flat when the pairs disagree. The lag is applied once to the blended signal.
  • Carry-Momentum (V3): sign of the 20-day change in the same slope, blended across the same two tenor pairs by the same sign-vote rule.
  • Value: F3 price against its own 1,260-day average, long below -10%, short above +10%.

Tenor pairs

  • Metals and Energy: F1-F3 and F1-F13. NGL: F2-F4 and F2-F14.
  • Precious: F1-F2 plus a long pair about 12 months out: Gold F1-F7, Silver F1-F6, Platinum F1-F5, Palladium F1-F5.
  • Agriculture: F1-F2 plus a long pair about 12 months out: Corn F1-F6, Wheat F1-F6, Soybean F1-F8, Soybean Oil F1-F8 (10 to 11 months, the deepest column in the file), Coffee F1-F6, Sugar F1-F5.

Rolling

  • New rule: each contract is rolled on the 5th trading day of the month in which its last trade date falls (previously: 5 trading days before the last trade date). The bridge on the day after the last trade date, when the data's F1 switches contract, is unchanged. In practice this rolls about 14 to 16 trading days before expiry for Energy, NGL, Precious and Sugar, about 6 for Metals, and about 5 for Corn, Wheat and Soybeans. On every contract tested the roll falls before the last trade date, apart from one contract where the roll was moved to the day before it.
  • Contracts whose last trade date is after the last price date no longer produce a spurious roll in the final week (the previous rule snapped them to the last price date).

How things are combined

  • Products inside a sleeve are equally weighted on common dates (a dropped date's move is carried into the next shared date).
  • Each asset-class portfolio combines its four sleeves by EW PORT (equal weight) or Inverse Vol (weights from each sleeve's trailing 63-day volatility, recomputed daily).
  • Combined books are two-stage: sleeves into an asset-class portfolio, then the five asset-class portfolios into one book; all four EW / Inverse Vol pairs are shown, with and without NatGas. Cross-pair portfolios blend two asset classes' portfolios the same way. Series are aligned on common dates before weighting.

Data and calendars

  • Prices: data/Prices_0924, all five asset classes through 2026-09-23 (previously June 30 for four of them). Reporting still starts 2011-01-01, so 2026 year-to-date now covers nearly nine months.
  • NGL labels (verified): the 24-Sep NGL file relabels its Argus sheets, and those sheet names are wrong; the underlying series are identical to the July file, whose labels are right. Checked against EIA's Mont Belvieu propane spot price (daily, via FRED series DPROPANEMBTX): the BAP series is propane (median price ratio 1.00, level correlation 0.995, 5-day change correlation 0.90), while the file calls it "Butane". CAP is ethane, not "Propane Far East": its 2012 average was 47% below 2011 (EIA reported ethane down 48%, propane 32%; BAP is down 31%), 24 cents per gallon on 19 Dec 2012 (reported 25 cents) and 13 cents on 16 Mar 2020 (reported 12.9 cents). DAE is normal butane (about 1.2 times propane; 2012 average down 10% against EIA's 5% for normal butane, allowing for swap versus spot) and IBD is isobutane (about 1.3 times propane). Products are mapped by ticker root: Ethane CAP, Propane BAP, Butane DAE, Isobutane IBD.
  • Gold and Silver deep columns (Gold F14 to F20, Silver F12 to F16) were revised in the new file from mid 2025; no pair used here goes that deep.
  • Roll calendars: Precious aligned to Bloomberg's contract months, Agriculture Bloomberg-matched, Metals, Energy and NGL on expiry_calendars_20260701.xlsx (it agrees with the 24-Sep consolidated calendar on every shared contract; those three were not Bloomberg-matched because no monthly files exist for them).

Checks

  • With the old roll rule, the new price files reproduce the old continuous series exactly through May 2026 (Gold, Platinum, WTI, Copper, Corn, Ethane, Propane, Butane).
  • Earlier versions of this analysis reproduced the August dashboard's Momentum and Value rows to three decimals for Metals, Energy and NGL.

Cautions

  • NGL tenors are provisional (F2 reintroduces heating-season seasonality). Platinum and Palladium F5 and Gold F7 sit beyond the range the liquidity study found fully liquid; Agriculture has had no liquidity study.
  • Platinum and Palladium F5 has data only from February 2010 (the monthly files have no earlier prices either), so their long-pair signals warm up during 2010.
  • All results are in-sample and not tested for statistical significance; the roll-rule change alters every asset class's numbers.
